notas.titulo: aws-emulator
notas.resumen: aws-emulator Finally, an official emulator from AWS to run tests against a local clone of their many different services without having to provision a paid API key to do so. It's written in Rust by a huge swarm of agents - 29,684 commits in the first three weeks of the project. Swaminathan (Swami) Sivasubramanian wrote about how it came to be in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog. It currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows. I'm hoping they fix that in the future - it would be great…

notas.titulo: Gemini Decisions API
notas.resumen: Gemini Decisions API Google join Jev and OpenAI in the decision model category with "Gemini Decision 1". This new model API is almost identical to Jev: it supports the same three types of questions (yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring) and even reuses Jev's term "Noul" for a yes/no question. It's priced the same as the GPT-6 Luna decision model: 10 cents per million input tokens, and output is free. Jev remains the cheapest of the three, at 4.2 cents per million. Jev is text (and JSON) only.…

notas_ingenieria.titulo: FLEX approach helps robots reason beyond literal commands
notas_ingenieria.resumen: Humans are intuitive by nature. We can sense meaning beyond the literal words that we encounter. Now, a new artificial intelligence–assisted learning platform developed by MIT engineers is enabling robots to read larger meaning into a human's natural language commands.

notas_ingenieria.titulo: Hybrid system could make cooling AI data centers cheaper and more efficient
notas_ingenieria.resumen: Data centers at the heart of the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution could be cooled more effectively and economically with a hybrid system under development at the University of Waterloo that targets hotspots on computer chips with a single drop of boiling coolant.

notas_ingenieria.titulo: Robots gain 'muscle memory' for planning their next moves in milliseconds
notas_ingenieria.resumen: If "to err is human," you could say robots are superhuman. They're more error-prone than we are, even when tasked with things like home and factory chores, which we might consider easy. One reason for these mistakes is that robots struggle to extract relevant details from the past and act on them in real time, even with vision-language models (VLMs), which interpret visual inputs such as videos and images along with natural language.

notas_ingenieria.titulo: New methods improve 3D scene reconstruction and robot mapping
notas_ingenieria.resumen: A research team led by professor Zhu Hui from the Institute of Intelligent Machines at the Hefei Institutes of Physical Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences has developed two methods to improve reconstruction fidelity, helping robots build more accurate representations of their surroundings.

notas_ingenieria.titulo: AI toolbox accelerates bioreactor simulations by up to 10,000 times
notas_ingenieria.resumen: The control of large-scale industrial bioreactors is one of the most complex tasks in the process industry. In the often huge plants, the smallest differences in temperature, pH value or oxygen content determine the success or failure of a process.

notas_ingenieria.titulo: PRISM helps robots move better by learning how forces and motion interact
notas_ingenieria.resumen: A new neural network component, developed at University of Michigan Engineering, challenges a common assumption in robot learning: that the same general-purpose neural networks used for image recognition are equally suited to controlling physical movement.

notas_ingenieria.titulo: Architected fillers: Shape becomes a design variable for composites
notas_ingenieria.resumen: In a recent study, researchers in materials science at Tampere University challenged conventional composite filler shapes by introducing a different approach in which each particle's 3D geometry is designed first, then printed to specification. The research enables decisions to be made on the shape of the filler, not only its material. This approach using architected fillers could pave the way for new solutions in soft robotics, biomedical materials with tailored stiffness and printed scaffolds…

notas_ingenieria.titulo: Green hydrogen production has a bubble problem—new model reveals threshold for steep energy losses
notas_ingenieria.resumen: A collaboration between researchers at Cornell and City University of Hong Kong has produced a new computational tool that could help overcome one surprisingly persistent obstacle to the efficient production of so-called green hydrogen: bubbles.

notas_ingenieria.titulo: Inspired by elephant trunks, shape-shifting robots bend, grab and team up
notas_ingenieria.resumen: Researchers at Colorado State University have developed a flexible robot that functions like an elephant's trunk to grip objects, with a goal of one day sending teams of these machines to aid in space exploration or to help with any number of other complex tasks.

notas_ingenieria.resumen: A small robotic frog developed at Aarhus University can swim using six artificial muscles activated by light. Behind the achievement is a systematic approach that could help researchers develop muscles for the next generation of soft robots.
